exact_claim: On a nonatomic normalized spherical volume, for mu>0 and 0<V=nu-mu²<mu², every finite L>0 is realized on some positive-volume shell by a strictly positive piecewise-constant profile with the specified first two moments. For a fixed 0<epsilon<1, strict positive feasibility is equivalent to epsilon L<mu and epsilon<=V/[V+(L-mu)²]; complementary constant/unequal-atom constructions prove sufficiency. Equality cases and V=0 have the restrictions in DERIVATION.md. Idealized moment preservation neither fixes a physical feature width nor guarantees real detector-count preservation when temperature/emissivity changes.
new_assumptions: The exact necessary-and-sufficient extension uses a nonatomic volume, already realized by the candidate spherical aperture, and allows unequal complementary subregion volumes.
The illustrative Lambda proportional to 1/T example is a mathematical positive response functional used to refute universal count preservation; it is explicitly not a claim about a real plasma.

limitations: Proof-only audit; no independent rerun of the candidate binary64 force table or its exact-rational program.
Rational moment parameters do not imply rational bulk density levels.
Variance bound alone is not the full strict-positivity feasibility condition; mass in the complement must remain positive.
Finite shell moment models do not preserve every radial enclosed mass, pressure profile, temperature spectrum, projected image or detector count.
Physical feature width is not inferred from instrumental PSF alone.
No real cluster solution, observational confidence, cosmological scale dynamics or gravity-theory closure is established.
Worker outcome requires separate orchestrator review and exact-hash acceptance.
